title: Crystalline LiPON as a Bulk-Type Solid Electrolyte

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper explicitly reports the target composition/formula as Li3.6PO3.4N0.6 (e.g., Abstract: “bulk Li3.6PO3.4N0.6”; Figure 2 caption: “b-Li3.6PO3.4N0.6”; Table 1 title; and text: “chemical composition Li3.6(1)PO3.4(1)N0.6(1)”). The extracted value “Li3.6P1O3.4N0.6” is not written in the paper and incorrectly inserts “P1” instead of simply “P” (implying a separate stoichiometric coefficient formatting that is not used).

The paper explicitly identifies LiPO3 as a precursor used to synthesize bulk crystalline LiPON: “prepared through simple mechanical milling of the low-cost precursors LiPO3 and Li3N…” (Page 3) and reiterates this in the conclusion (Page 5). However, the text does not specify the *amount* (mass/moles/ratio) of LiPO3 used; it refers readers to Supporting Information for further details. Therefore, the extracted statement “LiPO3 | Amount: Not specified in text” is supported.

The paper does mention Li3N as a precursor (“mechanical milling of the low-cost precursors LiPO3 and Li3N”), but it does not report the amounts used. However, the extracted field claims the chemical identity as “Li3N” with amount not specified; this is incomplete/misleading because Li3N is not the main product studied (the bulk electrolyte is b-Li3.6PO3.4N0.6) and Li3N is only identified as a starting material. Thus the extraction as written (“Chemical Identity and Amount: Li3N”) is not supported as the primary chemical identity; only its presence as a precursor is supported, and the amount is indeed not specified in the provided text.
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Chemical identity should be: b-Li3.6PO3.4N0.6 (bulk crystalline LiPON). If the intent is to capture precursors, list: LiPO3 and Li3N (amounts not specified in provided text).

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper explicitly states that the precursors (LiPO3 and Li3N) were mechanically milled “for 20 min under Ar,” confirming Argon was used as an atmosphere (chemical identity supported). However, nowhere in the provided full text is an argon amount/flow rate/pressure/purity specified—only “under Ar”—so “Amount: Not specified in text” is also supported under the null-handling rule.

The paper clearly indicates lithium metal is used (e.g., symmetric cells “Li|b-Li3.6PO3.4N0.6|Li”, “using Li metal disk”), so the chemical identity “Li metal” is supported. However, the extracted claim that the Li metal amount is “Not specified in text” is not supported because the text does specify the form/amount as a “Li metal disk” (even though it does not give a mass or thickness). Since some quantity description is present, “Not specified” is too strong.
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Li metal | Amount: Li metal disk (mass/thickness not specified)

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper explicitly states that the crystalline b-LiPON was prepared via a "simple ball-milling procedure" (Abstract, Page 1) and further describes preparation "through simple mechanical milling" of LiPO3 and Li3N for 20 min under Ar (Page 3). This supports the synthesis operation being ball milling.

entity_reviews.extracted_value: description=High-pressure low-temperature densification of LiPON powder

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper describes a processing route that includes pressing and sintering/densification. It states that the material is prepared via mechanical milling, then pellets are made by quasi-isostatic pressing at high pressure (e.g., 5.5 GPa) and elevated temperatures (200–450 °C) using a “high-pressure and low-temperature (HPLT) sintering technique,” and also refers to a pellet “sintered at 350 °C.” These operations match the extracted synthesis operation label “press/sinter.”

The source text explicitly reports the XRD/structure metrics. Table 1 (page 2) lists the space group as P21/m and the density as ρ = 2.38 g cm−3. The same table (XRD pattern section) gives the cell parameters a = 5.098(4) Å, b = 6.158(4) Å, c = 5.324(4) Å, and β = 90.60(4)° (the extractor omits uncertainties, which is acceptable). Additionally, page 3 reiterates these XRD-indexed cell parameters and space group. Provenance is broadly correct (Table 1 is sufficient); Figure 2a is not necessary for these numeric values.

The paper explicitly discusses the NPD/XRD combined Rietveld refinement for the bulk phase and repeatedly identifies it as b-Li3.6PO3.4N0.6. Figure 2 caption states: "Results of the combined Rietveld refinement of ... (b) the NPD pattern of b-Li3.6PO3.4N0.6." The text also states the overall refined composition agrees with "Li3.6(1)PO3.4(1)N0.6(1)". Thus the refined composition value Li3.6PO3.4N0.6 is supported (even if the exact refined composition statement is in the body text rather than only Figure 2b).

Both extracted SEM characterization statements are explicitly supported in the paper text. Page 3 states: “SEM images of the as-synthesized b-LiPON (Figures S1a and S1b …) revealed … sizes ranging from 0.1 μm to 1 μm…”. Page 4 states: “The morphology of the surface and cross section of the HPLT bodies observed by SEM (Figures S1e and S1f …) shows a fully and uniformly densified structure.” The alleged provenance ‘Figures S1a–f’ is consistent with these statements (S1a,b for particle size; S1e,f for pellet densification).

The source text explicitly states: (1) “The 7Li solid-state NMR spectrum of b-Li3.6PO3.4N0.6 shows a single resonance…” (Page 3, referring to Figure 2d), supporting “7Li resonance: single”. (2) It also explicitly gives the 31P NMR site distribution: “PO4 (4.7%), PO3N (56.3%), and PO2N2 (39%)” (Page 3; also described as the attribution/quantification indicated in Figure 2d), supporting the extracted percentages.

The paper text (referring to Figure S2a) states that an exothermic decomposition with irreversible N loss occurs between 450 °C and 650 °C. The extracted values 723 K and 923 K correspond to 450 °C and 650 °C, respectively, but the extraction labels them as “decomposition onset” and “decomposition end” in Kelvin without the text explicitly providing these temperatures in Kelvin or explicitly defining them as onset/end points. The document only gives the decomposition range in °C, not onset/end values in K.
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Report the decomposition temperature range as 450–650 °C (or 723–923 K only if explicitly converted/allowed), with metric phrased as “decomposition occurs between 450 and 650 °C (irreversible N loss)” rather than explicit onset/end in K.

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper text supports several elements but not the extracted ionic conductivity value at 343 K. Specifically, it states conductivity reaches 6.5 × 10−6 S cm−1 at 70 °C (343 K) for the HPLT pellet (page 4) and also reports 5.0 × 10−6 S cm−1 at 70 °C (abstract and conclusion). Thus the extracted 5e-06 S cm−1 at 343 K is not uniquely/explicitly supported as the EIS value at 70 °C in the main EIS discussion; the explicit EIS number there is 6.5 × 10−6 S cm−1. The activation energy 0.55 eV is explicitly stated (page 4; Table S2). The conductivity at 25 °C of 3.0 × 10−7 S cm−1 is explicitly stated in the conclusion (page 5), though page 4 also gives other 25 °C values (5.6 × 10−8 for low-pressure pellet; order-of-magnitude higher for HPLT).
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Use: ionic conductivity = 6.5e-06 S cm−1 at 343 K (70 °C) for the HPLT pellet (Figure 3a discussion). Keep activation energy = 0.55 eV. For 25 °C conductivity, 3.0e-07 S cm−1 is supported (conclusion), but ensure it refers to the HPLT dense pellets, not the low-pressure pellet (5.6e-08 S cm−1 at 25 °C).

This supports the extracted stability window of −0.15 to 5 V vs Li/Li+ and oxidative current of 12 nA cm−2 (as an upper bound).

The text describing Figure 3c explicitly states: “35 cycles (140 h)” and “overpotential of ca. 180 mV in both directions” during prolonged galvanostatic cycling in a symmetric Li|b-Li3.6PO3.4N0.6|Li cell. This directly supports the extracted cycle count, total time, and overpotential values (units and approximate wording match).
